examples.title: Worked application: Processes and threads
steps: A process provides an execution and resource-protection context; threads within a process typically share its address space and process resources while maintaining their own execution state and stacks. Sharing can reduce communication overhead but creates synchronisation concerns. Context switching and concurrency are distinct from true parallel execution on multiple cores.

practiceQuestions.explanation: Threads in one process usually share memory and resources, but each has its own execution state.

examples.title: Worked application: Synchronisation and deadlocks
steps: A race condition occurs when the outcome depends on uncontrolled timing of concurrent operations. A mutex can protect a critical section, but lock ordering and scope matter. Deadlock requires a cycle of waiting conditions; the classic conditions are mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no pre-emption, and circular wait.

examples.title: Worked application: Virtual memory
steps: Virtual memory gives each process a logical address space that the operating system maps to physical memory. Paging divides address spaces into fixed-size pages and physical memory into frames. A page fault occurs when a referenced page is not currently mapped as required; it may trigger loading, protection handling, or an invalid-access response.
